title: The Priest with the Golden Rook
body: Long ago in Spain, King Philip the Second loved chess so much that he made a priest named Ruy Lopez his royal advisor. Lopez was such an amazing player that the king rewarded him with a beautiful golden chain to wear around his neck. Hanging from this special chain was a tiny, shiny chess rook!

variants.lucy: Deep inside a quiet Spanish palace, King Philip spent his days studying the chess board. He found a wonderful partner in a priest named Ruy Lopez, who played with great patience and care. To thank his friend, the king placed a beautiful golden chain around the priest's neck. Hanging from the links was a tiny, polished rook that caught the soft candlelight.
variants.luca: King Philip of Spain was absolutely wild about chess, and he wanted the cleverest player in the land to help him run the kingdom. That champion was a priest named Ruy Lopez, who defeated everyone with his brilliant moves. To celebrate these victories, the king gave him an awesome treasure to wear. It was a heavy golden chain featuring a miniature, sparkling rook as the ultimate trophy.

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath
